memoryCompaction.recoveryBoundary: Valid journals roll forward; corrupt after-images roll back to the valid before-image; corrupt before-images retain the journal and enter REPAIR.
memoryCompaction.authorityBoundary: Compaction journals, receipts, generations, and repair state are non-canonical and all tested paths preserve the canonical hash.

deferredDelivery.timeBoundary: TTL uses deterministic scheduler-drain epochs, not wall-clock time or canonical world revision.

benchmark.boundary: Existing local three-mode wall-clock microbenchmark only; deferred-mailbox and compaction-recovery timing are not measured.

claimBoundary: Compaction interruption is injected at deterministic in-memory stages and then captured through JSON persistence.
The proof does not cover process termination during the physical act of writing a snapshot file.
A corrupt-before journal is not automatically reconstructed without another trusted source.
Recipient lifecycle and deferred delivery are implemented only for the current SOUND handoff proof.
Busy state is simulated through deterministic wakeState, not genuine concurrent execution.
Queue or mailbox capacity overflow is explicit but dropped work is not losslessly recoverable.
JSON persistence is not crash-atomic durable storage.
No performance or massive-world scaling claim is established.
Specialists remain proposal-only and are not independent workers.
